title: Blackjack Side Bets in Canada: Perfect Pairs and 21+3
excerpt: How blackjack side bets like Perfect Pairs and 21+3 work in Canada, why they cost more than the main hand, and when they are worth playing.
author: Lisa Davids
bodyHtml:
Open almost any online blackjack lobby in Canada and you will see tables with extra boxes next to the main bet: Perfect Pairs, 21+3, Lucky Ladies and similar options. These blackjack side bets promise big payouts for small stakes, and they are undeniably fun. They are also a different product from the blackjack you are playing. This guide explains how blackjack side bets work in Canada, why their house edges differ from the main game, and how to decide whether they deserve a place in your session.

What blackjack side bets are

A side bet is an optional wager placed alongside your main hand. It is resolved separately, usually based on your first two cards, the dealer's upcard or a combination of the two. You can win the side bet and lose the hand, or the other way around. Because the outcome depends on the initial cards rather than on how you play the hand, no amount of strategy skill changes the result of a side bet once it is placed.

That independence matters. The core appeal of blackjack for knowledgeable players is that good decisions reduce the house edge. Side bets remove that lever. You are simply betting on a card combination at a fixed payout table. If you are new to the base game, start with our blackjack guide so you understand what the main bet is doing before adding extras.

The most common side bets explained

Perfect Pairs

Perfect Pairs pays when your first two cards form a pair. The payout usually increases depending on how closely the pair matches: a mixed pair (same rank, different colour) pays least, a coloured pair (same rank and colour) pays more, and a perfect pair (identical rank and suit) pays most. Exact payouts vary by game provider and table, so always read the paytable inside the game rather than assuming.

21+3

The 21+3 side bet treats your first two cards plus the dealer's upcard as a three-card poker hand. Payouts are made for combinations such as a flush, a straight, three of a kind or a straight flush. It borrows the logic of poker hands and gives blackjack tables a second source of excitement.

Insurance and similar offers

Insurance, offered when the dealer shows an ace, is technically a side bet as well. It is resolved separately from your hand and, for most players using standard strategy, is not recommended. Other variants you may see include bets on the dealer busting, on your hand totalling a specific value, or on a progressive jackpot that grows as players place the bet.

Why side bets cost more

The house edge on a well-played blackjack hand can be quite low, depending on the rules in use. Side bets generally carry a noticeably higher edge. The reason is structural: payouts are set to look generous, such as a headline multiplier on a rare outcome, while the actual probability of hitting that outcome is small. The edge also varies widely between bets and between providers, which is why comparing paytables matters.

This is not a criticism of side bets. Casino games are entertainment products, and an extra bet that adds suspense for a small stake may be worth the price to you. How to decide whether to play them

A few honest questions can help you decide.

  • Am I playing to win or to be entertained? If your goal is the best long-run value, skip side bets and focus on the main game with correct basic strategy.
  • Can I afford the extra cost per hand? A side bet doubles the money you put in each round even if the stake is small, and losses add up quickly.
  • Do I understand the paytable? If you cannot explain what the bet pays and when, it is not the right time to place it.
  • Is it affecting my main play? Chasing a side bet payout can pull focus from sound decisions on the actual hand.

Practical tips for Canadian players

Check the rules before you sit down

Online providers publish rules, paytables and limits inside the game information screen. Read them. The same side bet name can have different payouts at different tables, and a small change in the paytable shifts the value significantly.

Set a separate budget

If you decide to play side bets, treat them as a fixed entertainment line item, say a small fraction of your session budget, and avoid topping it up when it runs out. This keeps a rare dry spell from eating into the bankroll you reserved for the main game.

Look at the table minimum and the number of decks

Deck count and dealing rules change the probabilities of certain side bet outcomes. Even without doing the maths yourself, knowing that games differ is useful when you compare tables. The bottom line

Blackjack side bets are optional, exciting and almost always a higher-cost way to play than the main hand. If you enjoy them, treat them as a small entertainment spend, read every paytable, and keep your main strategy intact. If you are focused on getting the most from your bankroll, the best side bet is often no side bet at all. Whatever you choose, set a budget first and stick to it.
